claim: For every \(\gamma\in[0,1]\), let \(X_\gamma=(\mathbb R^2,\|\cdot\|_\gamma)\) with \(\|(x,y)\|_\gamma=\max\{|y|,|x|+(1-\gamma)|y|\}\). Then \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_\gamma,\ell_2^2)=\sqrt{2/(1+\gamma)}\) for \(0\le\gamma\le1/2\), and \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_\gamma,\ell_2^2)=\sqrt{2/(2-\gamma)}\) for \(1/2\le\gamma\le1\). In particular the distance is uniquely minimized at \(\gamma=1/2\), where it equals \(2/\sqrt3\).

correctness.rationale: The proof optimizes over arbitrary positive-definite ellipse matrices, derives diagonal form by exact reflection averaging, and reduces containment to necessary-and-sufficient strip and vertex inequalities. The one-variable objective is minimized exactly, including the \(\gamma=0,1/2,1\) boundary cases. No finite experiment is used for the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The family is an established one-parameter deformation used for exact numerical-index calculations. The Banach--Mazur distance to \(\ell_2^2\) is a standard structural invariant. The result gives the complete profile on the whole family, respects the published duality, recovers the square endpoints, and singles out the affine-regular midpoint as the unique Hilbert-nearest member. This is a natural exact invariant rather than an arbitrary slice.
